explicit_two_PAR_branch_alternative.why_parallel_equivalence_is_not_enough: For real parallel devices K=sum(K_i), phi_eq=sum(K_i*phi_i)/K, but this only holds at the same physical terminals. Retained NPCC aggregate endpoints/impedance have not been proven to equal those terminals/parameters.

algebra.nodal: B theta + C.T q0 + c_j lambda = p, B=C.T K C
algebra.flow_constraint: K_j c_j.T theta + q0_j + lambda = gamma * t_public
algebra.ideal_transfer_equivalence: With f211=t fixed, B_without211*theta=p-c211*t; two100->48 injections with P33+P34=-t give the same equation. All other AC flows and angle-based interfaces are identical.
algebra.units: gamma=0.30012075175285535 scales MW once. Impedances and 100MVA model base stay frozen. Output public-equivalent MW=f_model/gamma.
algebra.scale_caution: If the same physical B were retained, P_model=gamma*P_physical would require phi_model=gamma*phi_physical for proportional solutions; X_model=X_physical/gamma instead preserves angles. Neither identifies physical angles after an unproved network aggregation.
